Estimated talk: about 14½ minutes01 / 14
Speaker notes · 0:30

We will first show what changes when DINO's two teacher-side controls are removed. Then we will compare two fixes implemented in the repository. Our main accuracy result comes from a validation-selected standardization setting; the mutual-information objective gives a direct way to reason about both collapse modes.

A matching loss can reward the wrong agreement

The problem1:00

Teacher and student match predictions across two augmented views. With no labels or negatives, matching alone does not require the predictions to depend on the image.

Image
two views→Teacher target
view 1↔Student prediction
view 2

Collapse A · one code for every image

Each output is confident, but all images use the same code.

per-image entropy low · batch entropy low

Collapse B · uniform output for every image

Each image spreads probability evenly across all codes; teacher and student can still agree.

per-image entropy high · batch entropy high · KL can be low

Key point: low teacher–student KL means agreement, not necessarily useful image features.

Background: Caron et al., “Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers,” ICCV 2021.

Entropy is measured over the 1,024 output codes.02 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:00

The model can match views without learning anything useful. A constant confident output uses one code everywhere; a constant uniform output is also image-independent. These failures look different in per-image entropy, so we also track the entropy of the batch-average code distribution. KL alone cannot tell us whether the agreement is meaningful.

One network, controlled switches, fixed evaluation

Protocol1:00

Training and ablations

  • 50,000 CIFAR-10 training images; 10,000 test images.
  • TinyViT: 128-wide, 4 transformer blocks, 4 heads, 4×4 patches; projection head has K = 1,024 codes.
  • Four centering × sharpening settings; 20 epochs, seed 0, batch size 512.
  • 97 complete batches per epoch = 49,664 images and 1,940 updates total. The shuffled remainder of 336 is dropped each epoch.
  • Two random augmented views; the teacher follows the student by EMA.

Temperature and evaluation

  • Standard DINO: student τs = 0.10; teacher τt = 0.04. Disabling sharpening sets τt = τs.
  • Centering subtracts a running per-code mean; its momentum is 0.9.
  • val_knn(): last 5,000 training images are queries; first 45,000 are the neighbor bank.
  • knn_eval(): 50,000 labeled training neighbors, 10,000 test queries; k = 20 weighted cosine neighbors.
  • Labels enter training only through validation checks, never the gradient loss.
Reference results: raw pixels 45.7% · untrained network 32.0% · full DINO 48.8%. These are task reference figures, not substitutes for this notebook's returned values.
Training loop and fixed evaluation03 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:00

The architecture and evaluation are fixed. The trainer shuffles the 50,000 indices, then uses only complete batches, so 336 shuffled images are omitted from each epoch. The training labels are passed to the loop only so it can call validation k-NN every five epochs. Final test evaluation uses the prescribed weighted k-NN and is not used to select the configuration.

Displayed bars are not renormalized; entropy uses every code.05 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:00

In the no-sharpening row, the probability bars look almost empty because each code receives about one-thousandth of the mass. That is not missing data: the plot uses a zero-to-one probability scale and reports the full entropy. With neither control, the two image distributions are also nearly alike. This is a useful check against treating every collapse as the same one-code outcome.

The curves separate the two failure modes

Four runs · logged training batches1:20

Teacher entropy: confidence of one image's code distribution.

Batch entropy: breadth of code use across the logged batch.

KL: DKL(teacher ‖ student) on opposite augmented views; low KL is not a success metric by itself.

Metrics: per-image entropy, batch entropy, directional KL06 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:20

Per-image entropy and batch entropy answer different questions. No centering drives individual targets toward sharp peaks and also reduces the number of codes used by the batch. No sharpening moves per-image entropy toward ln K, while teacher–student KL approaches zero: the networks agree on an uninformative target. The KL is directional and compares a teacher target from one view with the student's prediction on the other view. The different teacher and student temperatures can keep KL high in full DINO.

k-NN values are returned accuracies, not percentages.07 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:00

The ablations support complementary roles, but not a claim that the system reached a mathematically exact collapsed state. Removing centering concentrates the batch on fewer codes; removing sharpening makes outputs nearly uniform. With both off, this particular run is still close to uniform. The resulting k-NN values fall below full DINO, but remain nonzero, so we describe these as collapse trends rather than a binary all-or-nothing outcome.

Our design question: can a simple batch rule replace both controls?

Part 2 · motivation0:50

The repository contains two custom candidates. Both remove the DINO running center and temperature sharpening; both were tuned with validation k-NN.

A · Per-code batch standardization

Normalize teacher logits using the mean and standard deviation of each code across the two current views.

one target transformvalidation winner

B · Mutual-information regularizer

Reward code variety across the batch and confident predictions for each image through one information objective.

explicit anti-collapse objectivemechanistic comparison

We keep the choice rule clean: select settings using val_knn(), then report the held-out test results without tuning on them.

Part 2: target standardization and mutual-information regularization08 / 14
Speaker notes · 0:50

The codebase contains two Part 2 approaches, so we show both rather than silently implying there is only one. Standardization is the strongest validation-selected accuracy candidate. Mutual information is a more direct way to express why both constant one-code and uniform-output mappings are undesirable. We did not use the test set to choose between configurations.

Fix A: standardize the teacher's batch logits

Selected by validation1:10
Teacher logits
two views→Concatenate
2B × K→Subtract per-code μ
divide by per-code σ + ε→Softmax
τ = 0.08
zij = (tij − μj) / (σj + 10−5)
pt = softmax(z / 0.08)   and   ps = softmax(s / 0.08)

What is implemented

  • Per-code mean and population standard deviation over concatenated teacher views.
  • center=False; sharpen=False; shared teacher/student temperature.
  • Best validation setting: column-wise std, τ = 0.08, K = 1,024.

Important limit

If every image has identical teacher logits, centering the batch makes all standardized logits zero, producing uniform targets. This is an empirical stabilizer, not a proof that the uniform fixed point is impossible.

Code: standardized_targets() → train_dino(..., target_transform=...)09 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:10

Here the mean and standard deviation are computed for each output code over the two augmented views in the current batch. Removing a code's common offset reduces persistent dominance; dividing by its batch scale lets the softmax respond to relative variation. Both teacher and student use tau 0.08. This transform does not guarantee escape from exact uniform collapse: if there is no batch variation, the standardized teacher target is uniform. We therefore pair the mechanism with measured entropy and k-NN evidence and state the limitation plainly.

Selected column-wise run · 116 logged training points10 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:00

The selected seed-0 history has low per-image target entropy, so individual assignments are sharp. Its batch-average entropy remains much higher, so the batch is not confined to one or two codes. The approximate effective-code count is exp of the entropy; it is a batch-level summary, not a count over the full dataset. KL remains appreciable because it compares the teacher target with the student on a different augmented view.

Fix B: maximize information between image and code

One objective targets both collapses1:10
I(X; Z) = H(P̄s) − meanimage H(Ps)
L = LDINO − 0.5 I(X; Z)

How the two collapse cases score

  • Same one-hot code: batch entropy and per-image entropy are both 0, so I = 0.
  • Uniform for every image: both entropies are ln K, so I = 0.
  • An informative mapping has varied codes across images and confident predictions per image, giving I > 0.

Implemented setting

Student probabilities from both views (2B samples) feed the marginal and conditional entropies. The selected configuration uses λmarg = λcond = 0.5, τ = 0.05, K = 1,024; centering and sharpening are off.

The regularizer is added to the cross-view DINO loss; it is not a replacement for the teacher targets.

Code: mutual_info_loss() and train()11 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:10

This is a single mutual-information objective, not two unrelated tricks. The marginal entropy term rewards using codes across the batch. The conditional entropy term rewards confident per-image predictions. A one-code mapping and a uniform mapping both carry zero information about the image. Maximizing mutual information therefore makes either constant solution less attractive than an image-dependent code assignment. This is an optimization incentive, not a formal guarantee for every training run.

The information objective also avoids uniform agreement

Seed-0 tuning runs0:50

Selected run at epoch 20: teacher entropy 2.52 nats, batch entropy 5.09 nats, KL 1.114 nats; val_knn() = 0.4566.

Eight seed-0 hyperparameter runs · notebook-generated curves12 / 14
Speaker notes · 0:50

The chart overlays the eight seed-0 settings actually evaluated. The equal-weight setting maximized validation k-NN among them. Its per-image entropy falls while batch entropy remains above five nats, which is consistent with sharp predictions spread across many codes. The final KL is not expected to be near zero: the DINO student and teacher see different augmentations and optimization continues under the extra objective.

Takeaways, limits, and where to show the code

Conclusion1:10

What the evidence supports

  • Centering and sharpening counter different trends: code dominance versus near-uniform teacher outputs.
  • Entropy, batch entropy, KL, and k-NN together are more informative than any one metric.
  • Column-wise target standardization gave the highest validation score and the best three-seed test mean in the saved runs.
  • Mutual information makes both image-independent solutions unattractive, but its test accuracy was lower here.

Implementation map

  • Training loop: train_dino(), EMA, temperatures, history, collapse_curves().
  • Diagnostics: plot_variants() for teacher stages and four-run curves.
  • Standardization: standardized_targets() and its validation grid.
  • Mutual information: mutual_info_loss(), training hook, and validation grid.
  • Evaluation: fixed val_knn() and knn_eval().

Bottom line: agreement is not enough; useful training needs sharp per-image targets and broad code use—and the representation still has to pass the fixed k-NN test.

Questions14 / 14
Speaker notes · 1:10

Our strongest supported conclusion is empirical, not universal: in these saved runs, removing each DINO control caused a different failure trend, while the custom methods provided useful comparisons. Standardization was selected on validation and gave the highest measured three-seed test mean. It does not prove that uniform collapse is impossible; the mutual-information objective expresses the two-mode argument more directly but scored lower.
